notes: Item 3 candidate (Boldt/Hempelmann cluster, Ann Thorac Surg 1990;50(1):62-68, PMID 2369230, results/item3_raw_material.md). Blocked on paywalled guideline text since first opened (2026-08-06) -- eligibility search could not confirm an institutional source within reach. Deferred, not rejected: the block is unresolved time cost, not a judgment that no institutional source exists. With seven weeks left to the deadline (ADR-037) and this candidate already having failed to resolve on two prior passes, a third attempt is not worth the remaining budget. Also moot as a Rehabilitation/Therapy-tagged candidate now that Rehabilitation is not an annotation domain (ADR-075). Excluded from rejection-rate accounting (ADR-078).

Item 7 candidate (Iwamoto/Matsumoto/Takeda cluster, Curr Med Res Opin 2011;27(3), PMID 21456887, results/item7_raw_material.md, likely superseded_without_current_answer per its own raw-material note). Its per-batch cluster slot (ADR-041) no longer matters now that Rehabilitation/Therapy is not an annotation domain stratum (ADR-075) -- the reason it was worth prioritizing over other queued work no longer applies. Deferred on time budget with seven weeks left, not on any finding about the candidate itself. Excluded from rejection-rate accounting (ADR-078).

Item 17 candidate (JAMA Oncology, Choi et al., entecavir vs tenofovir HCC risk, record 20361, results/item17_raw_material.md). This item is specifically valuable because it is a retract-and-replace case -- the correct gold claim is "cite the replacement, not the original," a structurally different failure mode from an ordinary void retraction (ADR-069). Deferred rather than drafted from adjacent evidence: doing so would lose exactly the property that made the item worth keeping (ADR-083). Reason for deferral: the replacement is not identifiable from structured correction metadata -- PubMed/Europe PMC link the original exclusively back to the paywalled notice itself (PMID 31021386, JAMA Oncol. 2019;5(6):913-914) as the "Retracted and Republished" record, and no institutional access has been available to read it directly (ADR-082). If institutional access to the notice becomes available, revisit.

Item 37 candidate (EMF nonionizing radiation exposure and ADHD, Li et al., JAMA Network Open, results/item37_raw_material.md). Fully researched and ready to draft -- a second Retraction-and-Replacement case whose correction changes the substantive conclusion, not just its precision. Deferred solely because annotation closed at n=28 (ADR-126) for schedule reasons (arXiv preprint target moved to mid-September) -- not a rejection, not a finding about the candidate. Worth revisiting if this becomes a longer project.

Item 38 candidate (prenatal dexamethasone/CAH behavioral outcomes, Wallensteen et al., Hormones and Behavior, results/item38_raw_material.md). Fully researched and ready to draft -- a third Retraction-and-Replacement case, resolved to proceed despite the original abstract being erased from PubMed (the replacement's own findings are readable and the gold claim rests on those). Deferred solely because annotation closed at n=28 (ADR-126) for schedule reasons -- not a rejection, not a finding about the candidate. Worth revisiting if this becomes a longer project.

Item 39 candidate (TURP/5-alpha-reductase-inhibitor bleeding, Bansal & Arora, results/item39_raw_material.md). Fully researched and ready to draft -- notable for a second confirmed synthesis-contamination catch (the most current candidate evidence source, a 2026 meta-analysis, pools the retracted trial's own data; a smaller, older, genuinely independent synthesis used instead). Deferred solely because annotation closed at n=28 (ADR-126) for schedule reasons -- not a rejection, not a finding about the candidate. Worth revisiting if this becomes a longer project.
